one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-05. No Broadcom print: Q4 FY26 is reported after the close on 2026-12-09 [6]. No Broadcom 8-K or release since the 2026-09-10 10-Q; later EDGAR items are Form 4s, Form 144s and a routine note exchange offer [17,18]. Today's +4.30% looks sector-wide: on the same Finviz table MRVL +6.01%, ALAB +7.72%, CRDO +4.86%, AMD +3.66% vs NVDA +1.15%, TSM -0.48% [15]. In-window events: Big-4 hyperscaler Q3 results in late October with the first numeric 2027 capex guides [16] (every 2026 guide went up, so a mild positive skew, but widely expected); the note exchange offer expiry on 10-19 is immaterial. FY27 consensus EPS drifted from $19.57 to $19.39 over 30 days [14], with no sign of an imminent revision shock. After a sharp run, a partial reversal is about as likely as follow-through. Net: near-symmetric lognormal around ~$379 (+0.4% drift) with monthly vol 47%/3.5 = 13.4%.

fair_value.method: Blend of 19x FY28 (Nov-27 to Oct-28) non-GAAP EPS $24.19 = $459.5 (65%) and a DCF of FY28 FCF/share $20.32 at 11% (10y 5.31% + 5.7pt), 3% terminal = $334.9 (35%): 0.65 x 459.5 + 0.35 x 334.9 = $415.9 -> $416 for Oct-2027. FY28 EPS assumes AI revenue $180B (management line of sight $230B), FY27 AI ~$115B per guidance.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 EPS $24.19 x 19x. FY28 revenue $235.2B = AI $180B + non-AI semis $18.25B + software $36.92B; op income $144.6B (semis 57.5%, software 83%); net interest -$2.42B; tax 16%; 4.94B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Hock Tan, Q3 FY26 call: 'In 2027 we have secured the supply to again double AI revenue to approximately $115 billion' (raised from 'in excess of $100 billion' on the Q2 call [10]).

Management: 'line of sight for fiscal 2028 AI semiconductor revenue growth to again double to $230 billion. Here again, we have secured the supply' [6], but Tan also said they judged the GW count 'conservatively' because shells/power limit how many of ~30 GW reach production. Anchors: (a) purchase commitments rise from $52,674M (FY27) to $72,952M (FY28), +38.5% [4]; scaling the $115B FY27 guide by that ratio gives 115 x 72,952/52,674 = $159B, a floor because later-year commitments are still filling in; (b) house capex base 2028 $2,255B [16]: $115B/$1,841B = 6.2% in 2027; $180B = 8.0% of 2028 (+1.8pt share gain, backed by Anthropic +10 GW and OpenAI >5 GW line of sight [6]); $230B would need 10.2%. $180B sits between the commitment floor and management's figure.
Q4 FY26 guide ~$4.3B x 4 = $17.2B, +3%/yr for two years = $18.25B.
Q4 FY26 guide ~$8.7B (Q3 $8,752M, +29% y/y) x 4 = $34.8B, +3%/yr for two years = $36.92B (growth slows as VMware conversion laps).

Q3 semis segment margin 61% [6]; Q4 implied ~60% (66% x $34.8B = $22.97B less software ~84% x $8.7B = $7.31B, leaves $15.66B / $26.1B semis revenue = 60%). XPU memory content and rack mix dilute a further ~2.5pt as AI rises to ~77% of revenue.
198.25 x 0.575 + 36.92 x 0.83 = 113.99 + 30.64 = $144.64B; check: segment sum reproduced Q3 (61% x 20.84 + 84% x 8.75 = 20.06 vs reported non-GAAP op income $20,095M [1]).
Q3 non-GAAP interest expense -$703M + other income $98M = -$605M x 4 = -$2.42B; held flat (debt paydown offset by no assumed rise in interest income).
CFO: non-GAAP tax rate for Q4 and FY26 ~16% [6]; Q3 actual 3,118 / (20,095 - 703 + 98) = 16.0% [1].
Q4 FY26 guide ~4.94B non-GAAP diluted shares excluding buybacks [6]; held flat ($10.1B authorization remaining through 2026-12-31 [2] roughly offsets SBC dilution).

(144.64 - 2.42) x (1 - 0.16) / 4.94 = $24.19. Management says it is 'very much on target to exceed $30 in earnings per share in fiscal 2028' [6]; our figure is 19% lower because of the $180B AI haircut and margin dilution.

11-peer next-FY forward P/E median 23.64x, range 15.32x-60.27x [15]; AVGO today 377.32/19.39 = 19.46x on FY27 consensus [14]. 19x is inside the range, 20% below the median: by Oct-2027 the NTM year (FY28) grows +25% vs FY27 consensus ($24.19/$19.39) against a peer median 'EPS next Y' of +49.9% [15]; plus customer concentration (six XPU customers, Anthropic expected largest in 2027-28 [6]) and the 10-Q backstop ($29B max) and $42B note facility [3,5].

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF/share $20.32 (0.84 x EPS); growth FY29 20%, FY30 12%, FY31 8%, FY32 6%; terminal 3%; discount 11% (10y 5.31% + 5.7pt); valued at Oct-2027

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 FY26 FCF $13,665M / non-GAAP NI $16,372M = 0.835 [1]; Q4 capex guide $1.4B (vs $532M in Q3) for semi capacity [6] keeps it from rising; use 0.84.
10-year Treasury 5.31% on 2026-10-05 [13] plus ~5.7pt equity/cyclicality premium for an AI-capex-dependent, customer-concentrated semi = 11.0%. Sensitivity: 10.5% gives $358, 11.5% gives $315.
House capex base has 2028 growth of ~22% ($1,841B to $2,255B) with a low case that falls below 2027 [16]; growth fades toward nominal GDP after the build-out peak.

FCF/share 20.32, 24.38, 27.30, 29.49, 31.26 for FY28-32 discounted at 11% (years 1-5) = $96.0 + terminal 31.26 x 1.03 / (0.11 - 0.03) / 1.11^5 = $238.8, total $334.9. Net cash built by Oct-2027 (FY27 FCF less dividends) is excluded; it is ~$1-2% of value and offset by unmodelled dilution.

bear.story: AI capex follows the house low path (2028 $1,265B, below 2027's $1,390B low) [16]: FY28 AI ~$110B (below the $115B FY27 guide), semis margin 59% (less memory dilution). EPS = ((110 + 18.25) x 0.59 + 36.92 x 0.83 - 2.42) x 0.84 / 4.94 = $17.67; x 15x (NVDA's 15.32x, bottom of the peer range) = $265, less the full $29B max backstop as a lab-default tail ($29B / 4.94B = $5.9/share) [5] = ~$259.

base.story: FY27 AI ~$115B delivered (supply secured), FY28 AI $180B (8.0% of house 2028 base capex); EPS $24.19; market keeps a below-median 19x for concentration and financing exposure; P/E $459.5 blended 65/35 with DCF $334.9 = $416.

bull.story: Management's $230B FY28 AI (supply secured per the call [6]) is hit as Anthropic (+10 GW), OpenAI (>5 GW) and Meta ramp and hyperscaler 2027-28 capex tracks the house high case ($3,160B in 2028 [16]); semis margin 56.5%. EPS = ((230 + 18.25) x 0.565 + 36.92 x 0.83 - 2.42) x 0.84 / 4.94 = $28.65 (management: '>$30'); x 21x (inside the range, below the 23.64x median) = $602.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount argued as persistent through the horizon on checked facts: (1) growth: at Oct-2027 the NTM year FY28 grows ~+25% over FY27 consensus ($24.19 vs $19.39), well below the peer median next-year EPS growth of +49.9% [15], and post-FY28 growth fades with the capex cycle [16]; (2) concentration: six XPU customers, Anthropic expected to be the largest in 2027 and 2028 [6]; (3) Broadcom stands behind customer financing: max undiscounted Backstop ~$29B on the first tranche and a $42B convertible-note facility to the same customer (none issued), 10-Q [3,5], with XPV aimed at >20 GW through 2028 [12] and further backstops unsized (CFO: 'deal-by-deal' [6]). No premium despite ~68% operating margins because the largest high-margin AI silicon names already trade below the median (NVDA 15.32x, TSM 21.83x) [15].

thesis_break_reason: ~13.2x FY27 consensus EPS $19.39 (Yahoo, 48 analysts) and ~12% below the $289.96 52-week low. Trading there would most likely mean the supply-secured ~$115B FY27 AI guide is in doubt (a cut at the 2026-12-09 print or later, a lab customer deferring GW deployments, a lease default that triggers the up-to-$29B Backstop in the 10-Q, or a 2027-28 capex cut toward the house low case), i.e. a fundamental break rather than 47%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 2 re-checked every figure at the primary source. Q3 FY26 8-K: revenue $29,591M (+86%), non-GAAP op income $20,095M, non-GAAP NI $16,372M, EPS $3.32, FCF $13,665M, 4,937M diluted shares, cash $23,975M, debt $59,419M carrying [1]. AI revenue Q1-Q3 $8.4B/$10.8B/$16.7B [9,8,1], Q4 guided $21.7B [1]. Call: FY27 AI ~$115B supply secured; FY28 line of sight to $230B and, correcting my round-1 claim, Tan says 'here again, we have secured the supply' for FY28; 'on target to exceed $30' EPS in FY28; Q4 report on 2026-12-09 [6]. 10-Q detail the recaps skip: RPO $164.6B (Q2) -> $179.2B (Q3), ~25% due in 12 months [7,2]; purchase commitments $52.7B FY27 / $73.0B FY28 [4]; the Backstop max ~$29B undiscounted and a $42B convertible-note facility with nothing issued [3,5] (the supervisor's finding, confirmed; the press '$60B syndication' and Anthropic S-1 figures are removed). The CEO's 2025 PSU maxes at >= $120B AI revenue in any four quarters of FY28-30 [11], far below the now-guided path. FY28 AI $180B (between the purchase-commitment-scaled $159B floor and management's $230B; 8.0% of house 2028 base capex [16]) with a segment margin build gives EPS $24.19; 19x = $459.5; DCF at 11% (10y 5.31% [13]) = $334.9; FV = 0.65 x 459.5 + 0.35 x 334.9 = $415.9 -> $416 (+10% vs $377.32). This lands close to the supervisor's $420, from my own segment build (61.5% op margin vs its 62%, net interest $2.4B vs $2.0B). Scenarios bear $259 (25%) / base $416 (52%) / bull $602 (23%) give a probability-weighted $419.5. The ladder is a lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.38/0.27/0.24 around 259/416/602): median ~$417, log-s.d. ~0.42 against 47% realized vol, P(>= $377) 0.60. Thesis break $255 unchanged. Research limits: one transcript host (Benzinga via Webull) for call quotes, cross-checked against Platform Aeronaut for $115B/$230B; Finviz values are delayed quotes on 2026-10-06.
